title: SLO commitment cadence and handshake checklist
creator: Emily Zhao
description:
Background: As Redwood scales Dedicated and Private customers, handoffs between Product, SRE and Eng for SLO commitments are inconsistent. This ticket creates a prescriptive 'handshake checklist' and cadence for initiative-level SLO commitments (targets, error budget tranches, rollback gates) and defines the artifacts and automation needed to operationalize the lifecycle in the Console.

Goals:
- Reduce ambiguity when teams claim or accept SLO tranches for new initiatives.
- Ensure pre-rollout checks (test telemetry, alerting, mitigation runbooks) are completed before canaries.
- Automate escalation when error-budget burn rate exceeds thresholds and link to initiative status.
- Surface explicit signoffs and timestamps in initiative metadata inside the Console.

Scope:
- Product playbook (handshake checklist, roles, cadence).
- Console schema additions: signoff fields, tranche snapshots, escalation hooks.
- Lightweight automation: Slack alert + incident playbook link + initiative state change on burn anomalies.
Out of scope: full enforcement gate in infra (separate Dedicated RBAC initiative).
acceptance_criteria: Playbook doc in Confluence created and approved by SRE and Eng (link in links).
Console prototype shows per-initiative SLO signoffs, tranche snapshots, and a visible 'commitment date'.
Automation rule configured in staging: when 1h burn rate >2x and projected depletion <24h, send Slack escalation and tag initiative as 'At Risk'.
QA checklist and a canary rollout runbook validated with SRE on one pilot initiative.
Ownership matrix and quarterly cadence published and communicated to teams.

Store tranche snapshots as immutable objects in console metadata to aid audits.
